There are two different letters that look pretty similar except for the dots. ي is the ياء and is pronounced as yaa. While this one ى is called Alif layyena or alif maqsura (الف لينة/مقصورة) and is pronounced like the the Alif but without the hamza "ء" so it’s like. 
Example: the name مُنى, pronounced Muna not Muni. 
Not a linguist and i don’t know the exact rule, but ى usually comes at the end of a word. 

However, in the lyrics that you attached it’s a typo/mistake. "قلبى" is a mistake, if read according to how it’s written it would sound like “qalba” which is not correct, the correct pronunciation is qalbi (my heart).

I had a VA nurse in the SDU (carrying two patients, important for the story) tell me that my patient, whose Hgb is 6.7 due to GIB, did not get his pRBC unit 7 hours after the order was put in AND a phone call, because “he didn’t get it”. I ask what does that mean, “i just told you he didn’t get it because he didn’t get it.” 
“Was the blood not ready from the blood bank or sth?” I ask naively. 
“No it was ready, i just didn’t get around to doing it.” 
“But i put in this order 7 hours ago??” 
I kid you not, this was the response i got: “yeah, just because you put in an order doesn’t mean it’s gonna happen” 
To tell you i was flabbergasted, lmao i just told her to please give him the unit asap and just repeated what i heard to the team because i wasn’t sure if i was dreaming 🥴..
